anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps authorization intact: option 1 is still framed as "Authorize discard and retry", the discard and reset to the last valid commit are gated on the human's reply, and no cap grant is offered. After also satisfies the replaced preserved fact: it states nothing was discarded or reset, names the restored row 1 cells and `pending:` tuple as the only working-ledger write, keeps attempts 1 / iterations 2 / cap 9 in the rendered snapshot, keeps implement active via option 3, and renders no done/stuck marker. Before fails the fact as now written only because it never mentions the boundary-rejection restore of target cells and the pending tuple (it explicitly says it did not read the ledger from HEAD and wrote nothing), so the replacement wording is what moves it. One caution for After: "Recommendation: 1" sits uneasily next to "nobody has inspected the uncommitted changes" in Before; it does not break the authorization fact since discard still requires the reply, but if you want the stop to read as purely awaiting authorization, keep "Recommendation: none" or phrase it as "if you authorize option 1, a hint about the colon/comma delimiter would steer the retry" so the recommendation never reads as pre-deciding the discard.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps both facts: option 1 still asks explicitly for authorization to discard/reset, no cap grant is offered, and the new lines 'No cleanup has been authorized or executed. Implement remains active.' plus the unchanged ledger snapshot (iterations: 2; cap: 9; row 1: open; attempts: 1) make preservation more observable than Before. Two drifts are worth tightening though. First, After switches 'Recommendation: none' to 'Recommendation: 1', which nudges toward the discard/reset action; the authorization boundary survives only because the trailing clause re-asserts it, so keep 'Recommendation: none - discard/reset requires your explicit authorization' to avoid any reading that the driver is pre-selecting the destructive path. Second, neither output states what the boundary rejection actually wrote (the restored target cells and the `pending:` tuple in the working ledger); add one sentence such as 'Boundary rejection restored row 1's target cells and the pending: tuple in the working ledger; nothing else was written, discarded, or reset' so the 'only tree write' clause of the preserved fact is shown rather than inferred. Also consider restoring Before's 'You may supply a hint' and 're-evaluate targeting before dispatch' phrasing, since After's 'then retry with a hint' makes the hint read as mandatory.
